summary: This article explains how computers learn patterns from labeled data, how AI helps people every day, and why its mistakes and bias mean humans must check its work.
introduce: Show the title “How Computers Learn: Artificial Intelligence” and give pairs one minute to predict, in one sentence, what the whole article is mostly about. Write three predictions on the board and tell students they will check which one is closest to the main idea after reading.

keyTerms.def: a step-by-step plan for solving a problem
to know who or what something is because you have seen or heard it before
a word or name that tells what something is

challengeTerms.def: the ability of a computer to do tasks that usually need human thinking
a way of building computer systems that learn from examples instead of following only written rules
a computer system made of connected layers that is loosely based on how brain cells link together

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that artificial intelligence does more good than harm? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain why people must check the work of AI.
struggling: Pre-teach algorithm, recognize, and label with pictures or gestures, then let weak readers complete a main-idea-and-details web with a partner.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses artificial intelligence, machine learning, and neural network to state the main idea of the article in their own words.
